title: A Trail for the Monsoon
premise: Coral Underhill, captain of the riverboat Kestrel, is hired by her old rival Dario Fenwick to salvage the Meridian, a wreck that sank with her father's fortune — and the truth about why he drowned. The job was sworn off after a betrayal that cost Coral her memory of one crucial night, and as she races the salvage fleet and the monsoon, fragments of that night return. She discovers Dario caused the wreck and hired her to find the ledger proving it before she does. In the final storm, Coral chooses to sink the evidence rather than sell it, paying the debt of survival with the fortune she came for, and steers home knowing who she is at last.
about_author: August Voss is the pen name of a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working inland waterways before trading river charts for manuscripts. Voss writes adventure fiction about people whose livelihoods depend on reading water, weather, and other people's lies.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Coral pilots the Kestrel through a falling tide, establishing her mastery of the river and her crew's loyalty, while a debt collector waits at the dock. Her POV; the beat is competence shadowed by precarity.

chapters.title: A Rival at the Rail
chapters.summary: Dario Fenwick arrives with an offer: salvage rights to the Meridian, the wreck everyone swore off. Coral refuses, but he names her debt. His POV reveals he knows more about her past than she does. Beat: dread dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: What Was Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Coral's quartermaster, Ilsa, recounts the night the Meridian sank and the vow the old crew made. Coral realizes she remembers nothing of that night — a gap she has never questioned until now. Beat: unease taking root.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Coral accepts the contract for money alone, telling herself. The monsoon forecast gives them six tides before landfall; the rival salvage fleet has five. Beat: the race begins, adrenaline over doubt.

chapters.title: Charts Drawn in Grief
chapters.summary: Coral studies her father's hand-drawn charts and finds annotations in a second handwriting she almost recognizes. Flashback texture through her POV. Beat: intimacy with the dead, first crack in certainty.

chapters.title: The Fleet at Anchor
chapters.summary: The Kestrel passes the rival salvage fleet — led by Coral's estranged former mentor, Captain Reyes. A tense parley on open water. Reyes warns her off in words that sound like protection. Beat: suspicion doubled.

chapters.title: First Dive
chapters.summary: Ilsa dives the shallows near the wreck site and surfaces with a hull plate stamped with a repair date that contradicts the official sinking report. Coral's POV. Beat: the past is lying to someone.

chapters.title: Dario's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dario's POV: he searches Coral's cabin for the ledger his late partner hid aboard the Meridian, the document that proves he falsified the cargo manifest. He needs Coral to find it first. Beat: villainy with a deadline.

chapters.title: Night Currents
chapters.summary: Running dark to outrun Reyes, Coral navigates by feel and nearly loses the boat; Ilsa saves them and demands the truth about what they're really hunting. Beat: trust tested under pressure.

chapters.title: The Fragment
chapters.summary: A near-drowning triggers Coral's first true memory of the lost night: her father alive, arguing with someone whose face is still blurred. Beat: grief weaponized into obsession.

chapters.title: Three Tides
chapters.summary: Storm signs early; the window shrinks. The rival fleet moves on the wreck ahead of schedule, forcing Coral to choose between racing them or a detour to save a swamped fishing family. She saves them. Beat: character defined by cost.

chapters.title: Reyes' Bargain
chapters.summary: Reyes boards under truce and offers Coral a partnership, revealing that Dario chartered two crews — insurance against betrayal. Coral realizes she is expendable. Beat: betrayal sharpened.

chapters.title: The Blurred Face
chapters.summary: Coral recovers a second memory fragment: the blurred figure from the night of the wreck wearing Dario's ring. She confronts him; he lies smoothly, but she watches him lie. Beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: Two Tides
chapters.summary: The Kestrel anchors over the Meridian proper. Diving begins in worsening visibility; Ilsa finds the strongroom but the air runs short. Beat: claustrophobic tension, the sea closing in.

chapters.title: Inside the Strongroom
chapters.summary: Coral dives herself against all advice. Inside the flooded strongroom she finds the ledger — and her father's final letter, addressed to her. Beat: awe curdling into horror as she reads the first line.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Her father knew the wreck was coming; Dario scuttled the Meridian for insurance, and her father died sealing the proof inside. The letter asks Coral to forgive herself for surviving. Full memory returns. Beat: devastating revelation.

chapters.title: One Tide
chapters.summary: Dario holds the Kestrel's crew at gunpoint demanding the ledger; Reyes arrives, and the two rivals' alliance shatters into a three-way standoff as the monsoon's leading edge hits. Beat: chaos, all debts called at once.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: The storm makes landfall mid-standoff. Coral uses her unmatched knowledge of the channel to survive what the others cannot, watching Dario's vessel break on a sandbar he never learned to read. Beat: survival as judgment.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Wrecked but alive, Coral holds the ledger — worth enough to erase every debt. Ilsa tells her the choice is hers alone. Beat: stillness inside the storm's aftermath.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Coral burns the ledger on the beach, freeing herself from the fortune and the vendetta it would ignite, keeping only her father's letter. Beat: sacrifice as identity — she is not what she salvages.

chapters.title: Refloating the Kestrel
chapters.summary: The crew, now family by choice, refloats the damaged Kestrel. Reyes, humbled, offers honest work; Coral sets terms instead of accepting favors. Beat: earned restoration.

chapters.title: A Trail for the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Coral pilots out on the season's first clear morning, the monsoon behind her, the gap in her memory closed. She charts a new route of her own making. Final beat: wholeness — the river knows her, and she knows herself.
